introduction.en: A linked list is a linear data structure where elements (nodes) are stored in non-contiguous memory locations, each pointing to the next. Unlike arrays, linked lists allow efficient insertions and deletions without shifting elements.
introduction.hi: Linked list ek linear data structure hai jahan elements (nodes) non-contiguous memory mein store hote hain, har node next node ko point karta hai. Arrays ke unlike, linked lists mein insert aur delete karna efficient hai kyunki elements shift nahi karne padte.

realLifeAnalogy.en: Think of a linked list as a treasure hunt — each clue (node) tells you where to go next. You can only follow the chain; you cannot jump directly to clue #5 without following clues 1 through 4.
realLifeAnalogy.hi: Linked list ko treasure hunt ki tarah socho — har clue (node) batata hai agla kaahan hai. Tum sirf chain follow kar sakte ho; seedha 5th clue par nahi ja sakte bina 1 se 4 follow kiye.

content.en:
## What is a Linked List?

A **linked list** is a sequence of nodes where each node contains:
1. **Data** — the value stored.
2. **Next pointer** — address of the next node.

### Types
- **Singly Linked List**: each node points to the next.
- **Doubly Linked List**: each node points to both next and previous.
- **Circular Linked List**: last node points back to the first.

### Memory Layout
```
[data|next] -> [data|next] -> [data|next] -> NULL
  head                          tail
```
content.hi:
## Linked List kya hoti hai?

**Linked list** nodes ka sequence hai jahan har node mein hota hai:
1. **Data** — store ki gayi value.
2. **Next pointer** — next node ka address.

### Types
- **Singly Linked List**: har node next ko point karta hai.
- **Doubly Linked List**: har node next aur previous dono ko point karta hai.
- **Circular Linked List**: last node wapas first ko point karta hai.

### Memory Layout
```
[data|next] -> [data|next] -> [data|next] -> NULL
  head                          tail
```

codeExamples.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.data = val
        self.next = None

head = Node(1)
head.next = Node(2)
head.next.next = Node(3)

curr = head
while curr:
    print(curr.data, end=' ')
    curr = curr.next
print()

keyPoints.en: Each node stores data and a pointer to the next node.
keyPoints.hi: Har node mein data aur next node ka pointer hota hai.

keyPoints.en: Linked lists use dynamic memory allocation.
keyPoints.hi: Linked lists dynamic memory allocation use karti hain.

keyPoints.en: Random access is O(n) — you must traverse from head.
keyPoints.hi: Random access O(n) hai — head se traverse karna padta hai.

timeComplexity.insert: O(1) at head / O(n) at position
timeComplexity.delete: O(1) at head / O(n) at position

## Singly Linked List Operations

### Insert at Beginning — O(1)
Create new node, set its next to current head, update head.

### Insert at End — O(n)
Traverse to last node, set its next to new node.

### Delete a Node — O(n)
Traverse to node before target, update its next pointer to skip target.

### Traverse — O(n)
Start at head, visit each node until NULL.
content.hi:
## Singly Linked List Operations

### Beginning mein Insert — O(1)
Naya node banao, uska next current head pe set karo, head update karo.

### End mein Insert — O(n)
Last node tak traverse karo, uska next naye node pe set karo.

### Node Delete karo — O(n)
Target se pehle wale node tak traverse karo, uska next pointer target ko skip karne ke liye update karo.

### Traverse — O(n)
Head se shuru karo, NULL milne tak har node visit karo.

codeExamples.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, v): self.data=v; self.next=None

def insert_at_head(head, v):
    n = Node(v); n.next = head; return n

def insert_at_end(head, v):
    n = Node(v)
    if not head: return n
    curr = head
    while curr.next: curr = curr.next
    curr.next = n; return head

def delete_node(head, v):
    if not head: return head
    if head.data == v: return head.next
    curr = head
    while curr.next and curr.next.data != v: curr = curr.next
    if curr.next: curr.next = curr.next.next
    return head

def print_list(head):
    while head: print(head.data, end=' '); head = head.next
    print()

head = None
head = insert_at_end(head, 1)
head = insert_at_end(head, 2)
head = insert_at_end(head, 3)
head = insert_at_head(head, 0)
print_list(head)

keyPoints.en: Insert at head is O(1); insert at end requires O(n) traversal.
keyPoints.hi: Head par insert O(1) hai; end par insert ke liye O(n) traversal chahiye.

keyPoints.en: Deletion requires finding the previous node first.
keyPoints.hi: Delete karne ke liye pehle previous node dhundhna padta hai.

keyPoints.en: Maintaining a tail pointer makes end insertion O(1).
keyPoints.hi: Tail pointer maintain karne se end insertion O(1) ho jaata hai.

## Doubly Linked List

Each node has three parts: **prev pointer**, **data**, **next pointer**.

### Advantages over Singly
- Traverse in both directions.
- Delete a node in O(1) if node pointer is given (no need to find previous).
- Easier implementation of certain algorithms.

### Disadvantages
- Extra memory per node (prev pointer).
- Slightly more complex insertion/deletion code.

```
NULL <- [prev|data|next] <-> [prev|data|next] <-> [prev|data|next] -> NULL
           head                                       tail
```
content.hi:
## Doubly Linked List

Har node mein teen parts hote hain: **prev pointer**, **data**, **next pointer**.

### Singly se Fayde
- Dono directions mein traverse kar sakte hain.
- Node pointer diya ho toh node delete karna O(1) mein hota hai (previous dhundhna nahi padta).
- Kuch algorithms ka implementation aasaan hota hai.

### Nuksan
- Har node mein extra memory (prev pointer).
- Insertion/deletion code thoda complex hota hai.

```
NULL <- [prev|data|next] <-> [prev|data|next] <-> [prev|data|next] -> NULL
           head                                       tail
```

codeExamples.python:
class DNode:
    def __init__(self, v): self.data=v; self.prev=None; self.next=None

def insert_at_head(head, v):
    n = DNode(v); n.next = head
    if head: head.prev = n
    return n

head = None
for v in [3,2,1]: head = insert_at_head(head, v)
curr = head
while curr: print(curr.data, end=' '); curr = curr.next
print()

keyPoints.en: Doubly linked list allows O(1) deletion given the node pointer.
keyPoints.hi: Doubly linked list mein node pointer given ho toh O(1) deletion possible hai.

keyPoints.en: Requires extra memory for the prev pointer in each node.
keyPoints.hi: Har node mein prev pointer ke liye extra memory chahiye.
Dono direction mein traverse kar sakte hain.

## Important Linked List Techniques

### Fast & Slow Pointer (Floyd's Cycle)
Use two pointers: slow moves 1 step, fast moves 2 steps per iteration.
- **Cycle detection**: if fast meets slow, cycle exists.
- **Middle element**: when fast reaches end, slow is at middle.

### Reversing a Linked List
Iteratively: maintain prev, curr, next pointers.

### Merge Two Sorted Lists
Use a dummy head; compare and link nodes in order.

### Array vs Linked List
| | Array | Linked List |
|---|---|---|
| Access | O(1) | O(n) |
| Insert head | O(n) | O(1) |
| Insert end | O(1) amortized | O(n) / O(1) w/ tail |
| Memory | contiguous | scattered |
content.hi:
## Important Linked List Techniques

### Fast & Slow Pointer (Floyd's Cycle)
Do pointers use karo: slow 1 step, fast 2 steps move karta hai har iteration mein.
- **Cycle detection**: fast aur slow mile toh cycle hai.
- **Middle element**: fast end par pahunche tab slow middle par hota hai.

### Linked List Reverse Karna
Iteratively: prev, curr, next pointers maintain karo.

### Two Sorted Lists Merge Karna
Ek dummy head use karo; nodes ko order mein compare karke link karo.

### Array vs Linked List
| | Array | Linked List |
|---|---|---|
| Access | O(1) | O(n) |
| Head insert | O(n) | O(1) |
| End insert | O(1) amortized | O(n) / O(1) tail se |
| Memory | contiguous | scattered |

codeExamples.python:
class Node:
    def __init__(self, v): self.data=v; self.next=None

def reverse(head):
    prev, curr = None, head
    while curr:
        nxt = curr.next; curr.next = prev; prev = curr; curr = nxt
    return prev

def has_cycle(head):
    slow = fast = head
    while fast and fast.next:
        slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next
        if slow is fast: return True
    return False

def find_middle(head):
    slow = fast = head
    while fast and fast.next:
        slow = slow.next; fast = fast.next.next
    return slow

head = Node(1); head.next = Node(2); head.next.next = Node(3); head.next.next.next = Node(4); head.next.next.next.next = Node(5)
print('Middle:', find_middle(head).data)
head = reverse(head)
curr = head
while curr: print(curr.data, end=' '); curr = curr.next
print()

keyPoints.en: Fast & slow pointer detects cycles in O(n) time and O(1) space.
keyPoints.hi: Fast & slow pointer O(n) time aur O(1) space mein cycle detect karta hai.

keyPoints.en: Reversing a linked list in-place takes O(n) time and O(1) space.
keyPoints.hi: In-place linked list reverse karna O(n) time aur O(1) space leta hai.

keyPoints.en: Always handle edge cases: empty list, single node, cycle.
keyPoints.hi: Edge cases handle karo: empty list, single node, cycle.
